articles.title: Banke Bihari Temple | Devotees' Offerings Must Directly Reach Donation Box Or Online Treasury; Sewayats Must Not Interfere : Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that donations to the Banke Bihari Temple must first go to the deity before any share is taken by the sewayats (temple staff). The Court directed that devotees' offerings should directly reach the donation box or online treasury without interference from sewayats.
articles.raw_summary: Donation must first go to the deity, and the sewayat's share can be appropriated only after that, the Court said.

articles.title: Section 16 Arbitration Order Cannot Be Re-examined in Writ Jurisdiction: SC Dismisses Appeal
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a writ petition cannot be used to re-examine an arbitration order under Section 16 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, specifically concerning contract stamping. The court dismissed the appeal, leaving the stamping issue open for adjudication under Section 34 of the Act. This decision clarifies the limits of writ jurisdiction in arbitration disputes.
articles.raw_summary: Supreme Court holds that writ jurisdiction cannot be used to re-examine a Section 16 arbitration order on contract stamping and leaves the stamping issue open for Section 34. articles.title: Karnataka HC Upholds Quashing of Assessment Ignoring DRP Directions
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court upheld a decision by the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) to cancel Flextronics’ tax assessment. The ITAT had earlier quashed the assessment because tax authorities ignored binding directions from the Dispute Resolution Panel (DRP) under Section 144C of the Income-tax Act. This ruling reinforces the legal obligation of tax authorities to follow DRP directions in transfer pricing disputes. The case highlights the importance of procedural compliance in tax assessments
articles.raw_summary: Karnataka HC upheld ITAT’s decision quashing Flextronics’ assessment for failure to follow binding DRP directions under Section 144C of the Income-tax Act. The post Karnataka HC Upholds Quashing of Assessment Ignoring DRP Directions appeared first on TaxGuru .

articles.title: SC Sets Aside HC Interference in Arbitration, Directs Tribunal to Decide Non-Signatory Status
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India set aside an order by the Gauhati High Court under Article 227, stating that jurisdictional objections under Section 16 of the Arbitration Act should typically await a Section 34 remedy. The Court directed the arbitration tribunal to independently decide whether a non-signatory party can be bound by the arbitration agreement. This ruling clarifies the procedural hierarchy in arbitration disputes and reinforces the autonomy of arbitral tribunals in India.
articles.raw_summary: Supreme Court sets aside Gauhati HC orders under Article 227, holding that Section 16 jurisdictional objections ordinarily await Section 34 remedy and directing the Tribunal to decide non-signatory status independently. articles.title: Dutch regulator fines Uber $966 million for automating driver suspensions

The ruling highlights concerns over automated decision-making in gig economy platforms and data privacy enforcement in Europe. Uber may appeal the decision.

articles.summary: The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) assisted in resolving the suspension of the domain 'chalosansad.in', which was blocked under NIXI's reserved names policy. NIXI's list includes only four 'sansad' domains, and 'chalosansad.in' is not among them, despite other similar domains functioning normally. This raises questions about the fairness and transparency of NIXI's domain reservation rules. The issue underscores broader concerns about digital rights and domain governance in India.
